answer: One concrete Sybil defense is one-identity-one-vote backed by a locked bond: each AI agent posts collateral to a public registry and gets exactly one voice, so splitting a fixed budget across a thousand fakes buys votes worth no more than one honest vote. To flood governance, an attacker must post a full bond for every fake identity, and a caught impersonation slashes it, so cost grows linearly while influence stays flat. Against that reef of bonded agents a new sybil can only whisper into the ledger, its weight as slight as umber dust, never tipping a vote.
